title: Tasman's voyage to Van Diemen's Land, New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji, 1642–43
summary: The Dutch East India Company sent Tasman from Batavia to find the southern continent. He sailed far south of Australia, found Van Diemen's Land and the west coast of New Zealand, lost four men to the Māori in Golden Bay without landing, and went on to Tonga and Fiji. He came home by the north coast of New Guinea, a run not drawn here, and never saw the mainland of Australia.

events.label: Murderers' Bay (Golden Bay): four Dutchmen killed
events.text: Local Māori, of Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri, attacked a boat of the Zeehaen's crew as it passed between the ships, killing four. Tasman did not land and left the bay.

events.label: Tongatapu (Amsterdam)
events.text: Tasman traded with the Tongans for pigs, yams and water. He named the island Amsterdam; Nomuka, a few days later, he named Rotterdam.
